products.title: Brazil - Fazenda Angola - Natural
products.body_html:
Flavor Notes:  Nectarine - Pear - Praline

Producer - Silvio Carlos

Variety - Yellow Catuai , Arara

Process type - Natural

Region - Ilicinea, Sul de Minas

Altitude range - 1200 m.a.s.l

Nestled at an elevation of 1200 meters in Ilicínea, South of Minas, Brazil, Fazenda Angola is a small-scale coffee operation with a monumental impact. Managed by the dedicated Silvio Carlos, this six-hectare farm, with three hectares devoted to coffee cultivation, is a shining example of sustainable, agroecological farming methods. Silvio's profound respect for the land is evident in every aspect of his work, from enhancing biodiversity to preserving soil health.

Through the natural processing of this coffee, it delivers a beautifully balanced and lighter-bodied cup. Prepare for a delightful array of bright and sweet notes: nectarine, pear, and vibrant orange mingle with hints of berries, culminating in a comforting butter finish. This coffee truly reflects the meticulous care and sustainable practices employed at Fazenda Angola.

products.title: Brazil - Fazenda Barreiro - Yellow Bourbon
products.body_html:
Flavor Notes:  Cherry - Orange - Almonds - Milk Chocolate

Fazenda Barreiro was established in 1820 by Captain Joaquim Bernardes da Costa Junqueira, who acquired uncultivated land near the spa town of Pocos de Caldas in the southern region of Minas Gerais. The property later became a cornerstone of coffee farming, as his son, Colonel Agostinho Jose da Costa Junqueira, began cultivating coffee towards the end of the 19th century. Situated at an average altitude of 1150 masl in the fertile Sao Domingos mountain range, the farm benefits from the regions mild climate, ideal for coffee production.

For over 30 years, Colonel Agostinho's great-grandson, Francisco Otavio Lotufo, together with his family, has been committed to combining traditional coffee farming practices with a modern approach to sustainability. Francisco prioritizes preserving the farm's natural resources, including forests, water sources, and local wildlife, and supports 30 families residing on the farm.

Fazenda Barreiro remains in the family, now operated by Icato Agropecuaria Ltda. Francisco Otavio Lotufo and his son, Manuel Otavio Lotufo, continue to uphold the family's legacy. Known for producing high-quality coffee varieties such as Bourbon, Catuai­, Catucai, Mundo Novo, Acaia, Obata, and Icatu grown at elevations between 980 and 1300 masl, the farm has earned accolades in coffee quality competitions locally in Pocos de Caldas, across Minas Gerais, and on national and international stages, including the prestigious Cup of Excellence (7th place in 2004 and 18th in 2006).

Today, Fazenda Barreiro is committed to sustainability, dedicating 40% of its land to preserving native forests, springs, and waterways. The familyâ€™s dedication to environmental stewardship and worker welfare has earned their farm certifications from Rainforest Alliance, UTZ Certified, and Certifica Minas.

products.title: Burundi - Karambo Hill - Natural
products.body_html:
Flavor Notes:  Passion Fruit - Creamy - Milk Chocolate - 

Variety - Red Bourbon

Process type -  Natural

Country – Burundi
Region – Muyinga, Burundi
Producer – Smallholder farmer families, processed at the Karambo washing station.

Specifics – Like the Pulped-Natural methodology, Honey processed coffee is de-pulped to remove the skin of the cherry, and the coffee seed is allowed to dry with all of its sticky fruit mucilage intact.

TIB (This is Burundi) was born in June 2020, with ambitious plans. They acquired a piece of land to build their first washing station at Karambo Hill in Muyinga. The station started operating in the 2021 coffee season.

TIB’s coffee grows in Muyinga province in northern Burundi, a beautiful hilly region with an average altitude of 1500-1700m. It is close to the Ruvubu national park and crossed by the Nile river. They work with almost 2000 farmers with farms spread over 50 hectares. They produce fully washed, natural and honey Arabica coffees.

At TIB Coffee, they want their customers to enjoy the best coffee Burundi offers while knowing they’re positively impacting community life in Burundi.

TIB take a sustainability-focused approach to our production techniques to prioritise our land and the environment. They use erosion control and plant shade trees and leguminous plants that add nitrogen to the soil. They also grow bananas, maize, cassava and beans for biodiversity and extra income for the farmers.

At TIB Coffee, they help their farmers live a good life by producing the highest quality coffee they can. The vision is to make a true sustainable impact on communities and farmers, by forming strong partnerships around specialty coffee production.

products.title: Burundi -Migoti - Natural
products.body_html:
Kinama Hill, Burundi

High above Lake Tanganyika in the mountains of western Burundi, Kinama Hill is home to one of the country's most exciting coffee projects: Migoti Coffee Company. Founded with a mission to connect smallholder farmers to specialty markets, Migoti works directly with farming communities across the surrounding hillsides, helping improve quality, transparency, and long-term sustainability.

This lot is produced from cherries grown by hundreds of smallholder farmers cultivating coffee on small family plots between 1,700 and 1,900 MASL, where cool temperatures and slow maturation create exceptional sweetness and complexity.

Process: Natural, Patiently Crafted

Natural processing in Burundi is never easy.

Kinama Hill's unique microclimate brings cooler temperatures, more rainfall, and slower drying conditions than many East African origins. While challenging for producers, this extended drying period allows flavours to develop gradually, creating greater depth and complexity in the cup.

Process Flow

  • Selectively hand-picked ripe cherries
  • Careful sorting and defect removal
  • Slow drying on raised African beds
  • Frequent turning and moisture monitoring
  • Resting and conditioning before milling

The result is a natural coffee that balances fruit intensity with remarkable cleanliness.

Variety: Red Bourbon

Like many of Burundi's finest coffees, this lot is produced from Red Bourbon.

Known for its:

  • Dense sweetness
  • Elegant acidity
  • Structured body
  • Complex fruit character

Red Bourbon thrives in Burundi's high-altitude conditions, producing coffees that are often compared to the best of neighbouring Rwanda while maintaining a distinctive identity.

Cup Experience: Candy Meets Complexity

Kinama Hill Natural is a coffee that feels playful and sophisticated at the same time.

Expect layers of:

  • Red berries
  • Peach
  • Honey
  • Candied fruit
  • Cola-like sweetness

Underneath the vibrant fruit is a silky texture and soft acidity that keeps everything beautifully balanced. Many roasters describe a candy-like sweetness reminiscent of red sweets and ripe stone fruit.

Think:

Red berries, peach nectar, and honey wrapped in a clean natural profile.

Why Coffee Nerds Love Burundi Naturals

Burundi naturals often sit in a sweet spot between Ethiopian fruit intensity and Rwandan structure.

You get:

  • Vibrant berry notes
  • Bourbon sweetness
  • Floral complexity
  • Clean, refined acidity

Coffee enthusiasts frequently praise Burundi naturals for delivering juicy fruit character while remaining remarkably elegant and balanced.

Brewing Mindset

This coffee rewards sweetness-focused extractions:

  • Filter brewing highlights berry and peach complexity
  • Espresso produces rich fruit syrup and honey sweetness
  • Allow the cup to cool for additional layers of fruit and florals

The slower you drink it, the more it reveals.

The Bigger Picture

Migoti Coffee Company is proving that specialty coffee can be a vehicle for community development. Beyond coffee quality, the company invests in farmer education, financing initiatives, and local infrastructure projects that improve life throughout the Kinama community.

This is a coffee built on both quality and impact.

Sweet.
Juicy.
Distinctly Burundi.

products.title: Colombia - Coconut Lemonade - Purple Caturra
products.body_html:
Monteblanco, Huila

Some coffees are grown.
Some coffees are designed.

This Purple Caturra Coconut Lemonade from Rodrigo Sanchez Valencia is one of the most iconic examples of modern Colombian processing. Produced at Finca Monteblanco in Huila, this lot sits at the intersection of agriculture, microbiology, and flavour engineering.

Rodrigo has spent years developing fermentation systems that create repeatable and expressive flavour profiles while maintaining balance and drinkability. This coffee has become one of the most sought-after examples of co-fermentation in specialty coffee.

Process: Coconut Lemonade Natural

This isn't simply a natural coffee.

It's a meticulously controlled fermentation built around a custom microbial culture.

Process Flow

  • Selective harvesting of ripe Purple Caturra cherries
  • Creation of a fermentation culture using native microorganisms
  • Feeding the culture with citrus fruits, coconut, and sugars
  • Extended fermentation of the culture before coffee is introduced
  • Controlled cherry fermentation in sealed tanks
  • Slow drying under sun and shade until optimal moisture is reached

The result is a coffee that amplifies sweetness, tropical character, and citrus vibrancy while preserving structure and clarity.

Variety: Purple Caturra

Unlike traditional Red Caturra, Purple Caturra develops deeper coloured cherries and naturally higher sugar concentrations.

Higher Brix levels create the perfect environment for advanced fermentation, allowing Rodrigo's processing techniques to unlock extraordinary flavour complexity.

Cup Experience: Tropical Soda Energy

This coffee is unapologetically expressive.

Expect layers of:

  • Coconut cream
  • Lemonade
  • Tropical fruit
  • Lime zest
  • Brown sugar sweetness

Supported by a creamy body and sparkling citrus acidity.

Think:

Piña Colada meets fresh lemonade.

Bright. Juicy. Completely unforgettable.

Why Coffee Nerds Chase This Lot

Because it challenges what coffee can taste like.

The Coconut Lemonade process has become one of Rodrigo Sanchez's most recognisable creations, demonstrating how controlled fermentation can create entirely new sensory experiences while remaining clean and intentional.

This is a coffee that sparks conversation from the first sip.

Brewing Mindset

Lean into sweetness and aroma.

  • Filter brewing highlights tropical fruit and citrus complexity
  • Espresso delivers intense coconut sweetness and creamy texture
  • Allow the cup to cool to discover new layers of flavour

This coffee rewards curiosity.

The Bigger Picture

At Monteblanco, Rodrigo Sanchez has become one of the leading innovators in Colombian specialty coffee, proving that fermentation can be used as a precise tool for flavour development rather than simply a processing step.

The Coconut Lemonade project is a perfect example of that philosophy:

Experimental.
Intentional.
Deliciously different.

products.title: Colombia - Elkin Guzman - Natural
products.body_html:
El Puente, Huila

Nestled in the coffee-rich hills of Palestina, Huila, El Puente is more than a processing station—it's a bridge between smallholder farmers and the global specialty coffee community.

Launched in 2018 by Clearpath Coffee, the project was created to connect hundreds of local producers with specialty markets while removing many of the financial and processing barriers traditionally faced by small-scale farmers. Today, El Puente works with more than 200 farming families across the region, creating opportunities for producers to focus on quality while sharing in the value of specialty coffee.

Process: Natural, Huila Style

At El Puente, naturally processed coffees are produced with meticulous attention to consistency and cleanliness.

Process Flow

  • Selective harvesting of ripe cherries
  • Fresh cherry delivery to the El Puente station
  • Careful sorting and quality selection
  • Slow drying in large covered drying structures
  • Controlled temperature and moisture management
  • Resting and conditioning before export

The result is a natural coffee that delivers fruit-forward intensity while maintaining structure and balance.

Varieties: Colombia, Castillo & Caturra

This lot combines some of Colombia's most important varieties:

  • Castillo for sweetness and resilience
  • Caturra for acidity and balance
  • Colombia variety for structure and consistency

Together they create a cup profile that is approachable, expressive, and distinctly Colombian.

Cup Experience: Fruit-Driven & Juicy

El Puente Natural showcases the vibrant side of Colombian coffee.

Expect layers of:

  • Blueberry
  • Ripe apricot
  • Plum
  • Red fruits

Supported by a syrupy sweetness, balanced body, and a clean finish that keeps the fruit front and centre.

Why Coffee Nerds Love El Puente

Because it represents a new generation of Colombian coffee.

Instead of each producer carrying the risk of experimental processing alone, El Puente centralises infrastructure and expertise, allowing farmers to access premium markets while maintaining consistent quality. The result is a coffee that feels both community-driven and technically refined.

Think:

Natural sweetness + Colombian clarity + modern processing discipline.

Brewing Mindset

This coffee thrives when brewed to emphasise sweetness and fruit saturation:

  • Filter brewing highlights berry and stone fruit complexity
  • Espresso delivers syrupy sweetness and jam-like fruit intensity
  • Slightly higher extractions unlock additional depth and structure

Expect the cup to become sweeter as it cools.

The Bigger Picture

El Puente demonstrates how specialty coffee can create value beyond the farm gate. By investing in shared infrastructure, processing expertise, and direct market access, the project helps smallholder farmers participate more fully in the specialty coffee economy.

The result is a coffee that is both delicious and meaningful.

Juicy.
Sweet.
Built on connection.

products.title: Colombia - Ombligon Decaf - Nestor Lasso
products.body_html:
Origin: El Diviso, Huila

What if a decaf didn't taste like a compromise?

This Ombligón Natural Decaf from Néstor Lasso proves exactly that.

Produced at El Diviso in Huila, Colombia, this coffee is the result of years of experimentation by Néstor and Adrián Lasso, who transformed their family farm into one of the world's most progressive producers of rare varieties and precision fermentation. Together with producer Jhoan Vergara, they've become known for coffees that regularly appear on competition stages around the globe.

Process: Natural, Thermal Shock & Sugar Cane Decaf

Everything about this coffee is intentional.

Before decaffeination even begins, the coffee undergoes an advanced multi-stage fermentation designed to build sweetness, aromatic complexity, and structure.

Process Flow

  • Selective harvesting of fully ripe Ombligón cherries
  • Cherry disinfection and density sorting
  • Controlled oxidation
  • Anaerobic and submerged fermentations with recycled cherry leachates
  • Thermal shock to stabilise flavour compounds
  • Precision drying to 10–11% moisture
  • EA Sugar Cane Decaffeination at Descafecol

Unlike conventional decaffeination, the Ethyl Acetate (EA) Sugar Cane Process gently removes caffeine while preserving the coffee's sweetness, body, and vibrant fruit character. The result is a decaf that drinks like a world-class specialty coffee—not an afterthought.

Variety: Ombligón

One of Colombia's rarest and most intriguing varieties.

Ombligón (Spanish for "belly button") is named after the distinctive shape of its beans and has become highly sought after for its remarkable cup quality.

It's celebrated for:

  • Intense tropical fruit character
  • Floral aromatics
  • High sweetness
  • Exceptional response to advanced fermentation

Few producers cultivate Ombligón. Even fewer understand how to unlock its full potential.

Cup Experience: Decaf Without Compromise

Forget everything you think you know about decaf.

Expect layers of:

  • Cherry
  • Strawberry
  • Blackberry yoghurt
  • Sugar cane sweetness

The cup is silky, vibrant, and remarkably expressive, with a sweetness and structure that rivals many caffeinated competition coffees.

Why Coffee Nerds Love This Decaf

Because it isn't trying to imitate great coffee.

It is great coffee.

The combination of rare genetics, precision fermentation, and Colombia's EA Sugar Cane decaffeination creates a cup that retains extraordinary complexity while removing almost all of the caffeine.

This is proof that decaf belongs on the brew bar—not just the bedside table.

Brewing Mindset

Treat this exactly as you would a high-end natural coffee.

  • Filter brewing highlights berries and floral complexity.
  • Espresso delivers rich sweetness with a creamy, dessert-like finish.
  • Slightly lower brewing temperatures (92–94°C) can help showcase clarity and sweetness in EA decafs.

Take your time—the cup continues to evolve as it cools.

The Bigger Picture

Néstor Lasso is redefining what modern Colombian coffee can be, and this Ombligón Natural Decaf is no exception.

By combining rare varieties, advanced fermentation, and one of the world's gentlest decaffeination methods, El Diviso has created a coffee that lets you enjoy exceptional flavour at any hour of the day.

Innovative.
Expressive.
Unmistakably El Diviso.

products.title: Colombia - Pina Colada - Co-Ferment Washed
products.body_html:
Flavor Notes:  Banana Milkshake - Strawberry Cream - Pineapple - Mango

Producer - Rodrigo Sanchez Valencia and Claudia Samboni

Variety - Purple Caturra

Process type - Co-Ferment Washed
Altitude range - 1.730 m.a.s.l

Finca Monteblanco, a family-run farm in San Adolfo, Huila, is managed by Rodrigo Sanchez Valencia and Claudia Samboni. Sitting atop a mountain, its unique climate fosters the growth of exotic coffee varieties like Geisha, Pink Bourbon, Pacamara, and Purple Caturra.

Each harvest, Finca Monteblanco produces micro-lots that serve as competition coffees around the world. Coffees from Monteblanco are milled and prepared for export at the new, state-of-the-art Aromas del Sur dry mill in Pitalito.

Processing Method

  • Micro-organism Cultivation: Lactobacillus and Saccharomyces cerevisiae are cultivated separately before inoculation to each microlot.
  • Fermentation: The pulped coffee cherries are left to co-ferment for 150 hours with the micro-organisms with added fruit to develop the desired piña colada notes like pineapple, coconut, and liquor-like taste.
  • Finalization: Brix remains above 6 and pH above 4, ensuring balanced fruit notes without overpowering the coffee’s natural profile.

Please Note: No actual alcohol or liquor was used in this processing method.

products.title: Colombia - Sakura - Julio Madrid
products.body_html:
Huila, Colombia

Some coffees express terroir. Others express processing.

Bourbon Sidra Sakura does both.

Produced in the mountains of Huila, Colombia, this lot showcases one of the most sought-after varieties in specialty coffee today: Bourbon Sidra. Known for its remarkable floral intensity and tea-like elegance, Sidra combines the complexity of Ethiopian heirloom genetics with the structure and sweetness that make Colombian coffees so compelling.

The result is a coffee that feels almost impossibly delicate, yet intensely flavourful.

Process: Sakura Washed

Inspired by the elegance and aromatics of Japanese cherry blossom, the Sakura Washed Process is designed to maximise floral expression while preserving transparency and balance.

Process Flow

  • Selective harvesting of perfectly ripe cherries
  • Controlled fermentation
  • Careful washing and cleaning
  • Precision drying under monitored conditions
  • Stabilisation and conditioning before export

Every step is aimed at protecting the delicate aromatic compounds that make Bourbon Sidra such a celebrated variety.

This isn't a coffee driven by fermentation intensity.

It's driven by aromatic precision.

Variety: Bourbon Sidra

Bourbon Sidra has become one of the most coveted varieties in competition coffee for good reason.

It is prized for:

  • Exceptional floral aromatics
  • Champagne-like acidity
  • Layered tropical fruit character
  • Tea-like elegance
  • Remarkable sweetness

When grown at altitude and processed carefully, Sidra can produce a cup unlike almost any other coffee variety.

Cup Experience: Floral Architecture

This is a coffee built on refinement.

Expect layers of:

  • Cherry blossom
  • White florals
  • Peach and stone fruit
  • Citrus brightness
  • Honey-like sweetness

The cup is silky and structured, with a lingering finish that continues to evolve as it cools.

Think:

Geisha elegance. Bourbon sweetness. Colombian precision.

Why Coffee Nerds Chase Sidra

Because Sidra sits in a category of its own.

It offers:

  • The aromatic complexity of world-class competition coffees
  • Exceptional extraction clarity
  • High sweetness without heaviness
  • Extraordinary cup evolution

This is the kind of coffee that changes every few minutes in the brewer and every few degrees in the cup.

Brewing Mindset

Treat this coffee gently.

  • Lower agitation preserves florals
  • Moderate extraction highlights complexity
  • Filter brewing showcases maximum transparency
  • Allow the cup to cool and open up

This is a coffee that rewards patience.

The Bigger Picture

Bourbon Sidra Sakura represents the modern direction of specialty coffee: exceptional genetics, intentional processing, and flavour experiences designed around precision rather than intensity.

Elegant.
Floral.
Beautifully resolved.

products.title: Costa Rica - Las Lajas - Black Honey Milenio
products.body_html:
Flavor Notes:  Cacao - White Grapes - Crisp Apple - Mango

Produced by Francisca and Oscar Chacon of Finca Las Lajas, entirely of the Milenio variety of Arabica,

one of the rare first generation of F1 hybrid varieties that were created to save the coffee world simultaneously from mediocrity and climate change by crossing a tough, disease-resistant variety (in this case Sarchimor) with an Ethiopia variety admired for its beauty in the cup (Sudan Rume).

The traditional Costa Rica cup profile is classic, admired for its consistency, balance and immaculate freedom from taint â€” and often patronized for that same clean balance. One finds it accused of an absence of surprise, a lack of idiosyncrasy and nuance. For many coffee insiders, the traditional Costa Rica cup is the Honda of coffees, reliable but neither fancy nor flashy.

Justification for this reputation probably can be found in the respectable yet plain-tasting tree varieties dominating Costa Rican fields, particularly the compact Caturra variety. Plus there is the well-developed, sophisticated Costa Rica coffee infrastructure that performs consistent, centralized fruit removal, drying and grading without provoking taint, but without introducing the nuance often generated by small variations in processing or terroir. Traditionally Costa Rica coffee from various small-holding producers is bulked together by large mills, often owned by multinational trading companies.

MICRO-MILLS AND CHANGE

The classic world of Costa Rica coffee is changing, however, and rather radically. A newer generation of Costa Rican specialty producers has successfully injected variety into the predictable Costa Rica cup, often through unorthodox processing methods. If the traditional Costa Rica cup errs in the direction of predictability, some of the recent micro-milled Costa Ricas seem intent on almost recklessly asserting their unpredictability. Meanwhile, response to the epidemic of leaf rust beginning in 2012 is not clear. It conceivably could end by even further simplifying the basic Costa Rica cup through widespread planting of disease-resistant hybrids.

About the producer

The Las Lajas farm is nestled in the foothills of the Poas Volcano, located outside the town of Sabanilla in central Costa Rica.

The name Las Lajas comes from the Spanish version of an Arabic word for the indigenous-crafted stone artifacts found on the farm when it was first planted. In total, 38 hectares of land are divided into several parcels, each of which grow various shade tree species and create unique micro-climates. In addition, different lots process coffee differently some naturally, others either honey or washed. Las Lajas's farming diversity allows the farm to create several distinct products with different characteristics all within a contained area. There is a rich tradition of coffee farming in the Chacon family: generations have owned and produced coffee on their land for more than 80 years.

After the tragic loss of their father due to pesticide-caused illness in 1980, Oscar and Francisca made the conscious decision to do what their hearts told them was best for their family. The two began growing organically. This decision to grow organically was difficult at first because there were no premiums paid for organics at the time. The two risked financial stability. As pioneers, the Chacon family saw the value in building a healthier farm. Today, many farmers and cooperatives benefit from the risk Oscar and Francisca and other farmers took many years ago. Las Lajas was one of the first farms to produce organic coffee and remains one of the only certified-organic farms in Costa Rica.

products.title: Diego Bermudez - L-01 Castillo - 200g
products.body_html:
Flavour Notes- Ginger, Blood Orange, Lime - Clean and Crisp

Location:  Cauca, Colombia
Producer: Diego Bermudez/Finca El Paraíso
Variety:    Castillo
Altitude:    1,600 – 1,800 m.
Process:   Anaerobic Thermal Shock

Diego Samuel who was born in Bolivar, Cauca has dedicated the last 13 years of his life to growing coffee and to also gaining a deep understanding and knowledge on the processing and production of high-end specialty coffee that is almost unparalleled in the unique flavour and profiles produced.

As part of a tight knit family Diego works on their farm in Cauca with his family. Together they are involved on the pursuit of continual learning and striving to achieve the next level with their processing. They built their own lab on the farm to firstly understand about cupping and roasting so they could then start to curate their own fermentation protocols for them to begin experimenting with. These experiments and novel approach to coffee have allowed to him to soar and exceed winning several awards from 2015 onwards.

As well as being an accomplished cupped Diego has also achieved the CQI level 2 processing course qualification which allowed him to get a base for seeing how cup profiles could be guided depending on microorganisms, ph and temperature.

The Villa Esperanza - Paraiso farm in El Tambo, Cauca covers 27 ha of land and is planted with Castillo, Colombia, Caturra, Pink Bourbon and Geisha. The farm focuses on technology and the critical processes that and intricate in producing coffee of this mark. From the selection to the meticulous drying which is done in a way to mitigate the changeable climatic conditions allowing them to replicate coffees of such high standards.

All these lots selected come from the Castillo, which again disproves myths that still question the quality this varietal can produce when the treatment of the raw product is taken into such depth to draw out its light and true potential.


Process

  1. Anaerobic fermentation in cherry for 28 hours in tanks with relief valves at a temperature of 19o Celsius.
  2. Pulping of the coffee
  3. Anaerobic fermentation with a medium of cultivated mucilage for 40 hours at 21o Celsius.
  4. Thermic shock washed. First, washed with water at 40o Celsius and then water at 12o Celsius.
  5. Controlled drying for 28 hours at 42o Celsius and a relative humidity of 25%,until reaching a bean moisture between 10% - 11%.

products.title: Diego Bermudez - Pink Bourbon - 200g
products.body_html:
So floral and oh so sweet... 

Flavour Notes- Peach, Apricot, Sweet Milky Tea - Tropical Fruit

Location:  Cauca, Colombia
Producer: Diego Bermudez/Finca El Paraíso
Variety:     Pink Bourbon
Altitude:    1,600 – 1,800 m.
Process:   Double Anaerobic Thermal Shock Washed

Diego Bermudez and the team at Finca El Paraiso in Cauca Colombia are often known for their meticulous processing and inventive methods.

This is a very special Pink Bourbon variety coffee grown by coffee processing innovators Diego Bermudez and Finca El Paraiso in Piendamó, Cauca. Pink Bourbon was initially thought to be a mutation of the famed bourbon variety, but genetic testing has revealed it is a unique Ethiopian landrace. This coffee is processed using Diego’s special "TROPICAL YEAST" in an innovative multiple-phase fermentation with Thermal Shock method.

The process begins with proper harvesting of cherries at ideal maturation. The coffee is then disinfected/sterilized with ozone and transferred to cherry fermentation tanks. There the coffee goes 36 hr anaerobic fermentation. 

The coffee is depulped and the mucilage and pulp goes to the pilot plant to carry out the production of process-specific microorganisms and generate the culture medium that contains the precursos of aromas and flavors produced in fermentation. This culture medium is transferred to the fermentation tanks to join the coffee where they remain in contact for 12 hours under pressure. 

Then the “thermal shock” process is then carried out by subjecting the coffee to higher temperature water for a determined amount of time, then “shocking” it with cold water. This process aims to fix a greater amount of precursors and “seal” the coffee for optimal drying.

The coffee is dried using a de-humidifier to remove moisture while preventing over-oxidation, stopping any over-fermentation and preserving the coffee’s delicate characteristics.

products.body_html:

Producer - Los Naranjos

Los Naranjos Café is the merger of three great men, Sigfredo Corado, David Velásquez and Manuel Olivares.

None of them imagined that 35 years later, something as beautiful as coffee growing was going to bring them back together again.

These friends met in high school, all of them from different origins but with one purpose in common, overcome themselves.

The stunning landscape of the Apaneca-Ilamatepec mountain range, It's the largest coffee production zone of the country. This region has a special touch since here's where Sigfredo grew up also this place keeps David's most memorable memories when he used to pick coffee on the nearby farms.

products.title: Ethiopia - Bishan Wate - Natural
products.body_html:
Bishan Wate, Guji

From the highlands of Guji, one of Ethiopia’s most celebrated coffee-growing regions, comes a coffee that captures everything specialty coffee lovers seek in a natural Ethiopian profile. Produced by renowned exporter and producer Faysel Abdosh, Bishan Wate showcases the remarkable terroir of southern Ethiopia through meticulous cultivation and processing.

Grown at high elevations under ideal climatic conditions, cherries mature slowly, developing the dense sugars and complex aromatics that have made Guji a benchmark for modern Ethiopian coffee.

Process: Natural, Elevated

At Bishan Wate, quality begins with cherry selection.

Process Flow

  • Selective hand-picking of fully ripe cherries
  • Careful sorting and density selection
  • Slow drying on raised African beds
  • Continuous turning and moisture monitoring
  • Resting and conditioning before milling and export

The natural process allows the fruit to dry around the seed, intensifying sweetness while preserving the floral elegance that defines exceptional Ethiopian coffee.

Variety: Ethiopian Heirloom

Produced from local Ethiopian landrace varieties, this coffee expresses the diversity and complexity that make Ethiopia unlike any other coffee origin.

These heirloom cultivars are known for:

  • Intense floral aromatics
  • Layered fruit complexity
  • Delicate tea-like structure
  • Remarkable sweetness and clarity

Cup Experience: A Guji Classic

This is the kind of coffee that put Guji on the map.

Expect:

  • Blueberry and mixed berry sweetness
  • Peach and tropical fruit notes
  • Jasmine florals
  • Silky body
  • Long, sweet finish

The profile is vibrant and expressive, yet remarkably clean for a natural process.

Why Coffee Nerds Love Guji Naturals

Guji has become synonymous with coffees that combine:

  • The fruit intensity of natural processing
  • Exceptional floral complexity
  • High-altitude sweetness
  • Elegant structure

Bishan Wate delivers all of these characteristics while maintaining balance and drinkability.

Think juicy fruit, floral lift, and crystalline sweetness.

Brewing Mindset

This coffee rewards a gentle approach:

  • Filter brewing highlights florals and layered fruit
  • Espresso amplifies sweetness and tropical notes
  • Slightly cooler brew temperatures can enhance clarity and complexity

Let the coffee cool as you drink—it continues to evolve in the cup.

The Bigger Picture

Faysel Abdosh has become one of the most respected names in Ethiopian specialty coffee, helping bring extraordinary Guji coffees to roasters around the world. Bishan Wate reflects that commitment to quality, traceability, and the preservation of Ethiopia’s unique coffee heritage.

This is modern Ethiopian coffee at its finest:

Floral.
Juicy.
Effortlessly elegant.

products.title: Ethiopia - Eva Gotiti - Washed
products.body_html:
Flavor Notes:  Bergamot - Blueberry - Jasmin - Smooth

Producer - Eva Gotiti Washing Station

Variety - 74110, 74112, 7454

Process type - Washed

Altitude range - 2200 m.a.s.l

A fantastic example of all that is wonderful about Ethiopian coffee! This lot from the Gotiti Washing Station located in Gotiti Kebele has been harvested by approximately 868 micro-entrepreneurs from the surrounding area and is bursting with complexity and is almost tea-like in character! There are delicious blueberry and floral notes which make this a coffee best suited to paper filter methods and served without milk.

Gotiti washing station follows strict water management and traceability practices, reducing water use, separating coffee pulp from wastewater, and implementing efficient record-keeping from farm to export. Gotiti’s commitment to environmental and social responsibility is also exemplary, providing coffee seedlings to the community, financial support to underprivileged farmers, and premium payments based on coffee deliveries. These efforts not only enhance sustainability but also strengthen the relationships between farmers and the washing station.

As with all of our Ethiopian purchases, we also support import partner, Falcon Specialty’s, amazing ‘Stumping Project’ which has been established alongside non-profit organisation TechnoServe. In recent years, coffee producing regions have seen their yield (and therefore income from coffee) severely impacted. Agronomists have attributed this low yield to the ageing stock of coffee trees across the country which will continue to produce less and less cherries as time goes on.

‘The Stumping Project’ is a pilot study designed to test the success of the provision of incentives to encourage Ethiopian producers to stump their coffee trees. An effective tool in farm management that can help to breathe new life into a farmer’s crop and ultimately improve yield. Since 2022, your purchases of Ethiopian coffee have gone on to help 22 families rejuvenate their farms and increase household income. So enjoy this cup which not only tastes good but does good too!

products.title: Ethiopia - Girma Tamiru - Aricha
products.body_html:
Flavor Notes:  Raspberry - Tropical Fruit - Cola - Rich Chocolate


The high altitude and the natural anaerobic process intersect to make a wild and vibrant cup, with plenty of tropical layers.

THE REVIVAL OF ARICHA

The Aricha Coffee Washing Station is located about 5km from Yirgacheffe the capital of a district with the same name that is very well known for its coffee. In addition to an ideal climate and geography, the population has a strong connection with coffee production: here, it grows wild in the native forests, and families have been picking, selling and consuming it for centuries now.

Aricha was first established in 2000 back then, it was known as Adorsi. Despite ideal growing conditions, the management didn't seem to take off; within a decade, the site was almost abandoned.

In 2018, Faysel Abdosh from Testi Coffee acquired the station to revive the area, bring back value to the community and showcase the fantastic coffee growing in its surroundings. While technically not a cooperative, it works as such; producers from the Aricha, Reko, Gersi and Naga Singache neighbourhoods bring their cherries in, and those get processed and sold independently under each name.

Since Testi took over, they've contributed to local projects (like building a school and bringing electricity to producers homes). Also, they have put Aricha coffee back on the map: in 2019, just one year after reviving the station, four of their coffees made The Ethiopian Cup.

products.title: Kenya - Karuthi AB - Washed
products.body_html:
Flavor Notes:  Grape Fruit - Apricot - Lemon - Soft Mouthfeel

Nyeri County features cool temperatures and fertile central highlands. It lies between the eastern base of the Aberdare (Nyandarua) Range, part of the eastern end of the Great Rift Valley, and the western slopes of Mt. Kenya. Nyeri town, the county headquarters, serves as a destination for visitors to Aberdare National Park and Mt. Kenya. The region's fertile soil, seasonal rainfall, and high altitude create an ideal climate for coffee cultivation. This environment produces coffees with high acidity, full body, and ripe fruit flavors. The cool nighttime temperatures at high altitudes cause the coffee beans to develop slowly, resulting in dense, hard beans with high acidity and complexity.

Built in the 1980s between the Rwarai and Chinga rivers, Karuthi is one of the younger factories in Othaya, and its production volume is typically lower than most of the other neighbouring factories. This lower quantity of cherry makes quality control a bit easier during the peak of the harvest.

To produce this lot, the ~400 farmer members of the co-operative will contribute their coffee. It will then be pulped, before allowing them to ferment for 12-48 hours depending on the weather, then they will be washed to remove the last of the mucilage. After this, the beans are dried on raised African beds over the course of 2-3 weeks until the moisture level is about 12%. The co-op has a dry mill where the beans are rested in parchment for 3 weeks before hulling, cleaning and grading by size.

products.title: Kenya - Kiandu AB - Washed
products.body_html:
Origin: Kiambu Precision

This coffee comes from Kiandu Factory in Kiambu County, one of Kenya’s most technically consistent and quality-driven coffee regions. Situated just north of Nairobi, Kiambu is known for high elevations, cool nights, and volcanic soils — conditions that slow cherry development and concentrate acidity, sugars, and aromatics.

This lot represents Kenya doing what it does best: clarity, structure, and intensity — without shortcuts.

Process: Washed, But Hyper-Dialled

Kiandu AB is fully washed using Kenya’s classic multi-stage wet processing — a method refined over decades to maximise cleanliness and cup definition.

Process Flow

  • Hand-picked, ripe cherry selection

  • Depulped and fermented under water

  • Thorough washed channel grading

  • Slow sun drying on raised beds

Nothing experimental here — just extreme process discipline. Every step is about preserving transparency and showcasing terroir rather than fermentation character.

Varieties: Kenyan Royalty

Primarily SL28 and SL34, Kenya’s most iconic cultivars.

These varieties are famous for:

  • High phosphoric acidity

  • Blackcurrant and citrus intensity

  • Exceptional structure and longevity in the cup

They don’t hide flaws — which is exactly why they’re used when quality is high.

Cup Experience: Laser-Focused Brightness

SCA 88 points puts this lot firmly into elite territory. Expect a cup that is:

  • High-definition acidity

  • Clean, articulate sweetness

  • Long, resonant finish

Think less “wild” and more architectural — flavour elements stacked cleanly, each note distinct, nothing muddy.

This is a coffee that tastes intentional.

Why Coffee Nerds Chase Kenyan AB Lots

Because size grade + processing + terroir alignment matters.

AB screen size often delivers:

  • Slightly faster extraction

  • Sharper acidity expression

  • Increased aromatic lift

When paired with strong processing, AB lots like this can feel more electric and dynamic than larger screens.

Brewing Mindset

Treat this like a high-acidity, high-clarity coffee:

  • Higher brew ratios → unlock complexity

  • Slightly finer grind → increase sweetness

  • Avoid under-extraction — this coffee wants energy

Filter methods shine brightest, but a tight espresso can be spectacularly vibrant.

The Bigger Picture

Kenya Kiandu AB is a reminder that washed coffees don’t need reinvention — just respect, precision, and patience.

No fermentation theatrics.
No trend chasing.

Just one of the world’s most refined coffee systems, operating exactly as intended.

products.title: Kenya - Kii AA - Washed
products.body_html:
Flavor Notes:  Sweet Orange - Caramel - Lime - Bright Acidity


Kii Factory is one of three owned and operated by Rungeto Farmers Cooperative Society (FCS). Rungeto has over 850 members, many of whom deliver cherry to Kii. The factory itself was constructed in 1995, nestled at the foot of Mt. Kenya. The Kii River, which runs nearby, gives the factory both its name and clean water for washing fine, Fully washed coffees.

In recent years, great efforts have been made to improve and ensure coffee quality from Kii. These measures are evident in the consistently complex and clean coffees produced.

Harvest & Post-Harvest


Smallholders selectively handpick only ripe cherry and deliver it to Kii Factory. At intake, the Cherry Clerk oversees meticulous visual sorting, accepting only dense, ripe cherry. The quality for which Kii coffee is known is directly impacted by this stringent approach to detail.

After intake, cherry is pulped and fermented for approximately 16-24 hours, depending on ambient temperature at the time. Following fermentation, coffee is washed in clean water from the Kii River and soaked for 12 hours. Newly installed tiles in the washing channels help preserve coffee and water quality, and all water used in processing is also cleaned by filtering in earthen pits before being reintroduced to local waterways.

After washing and grading, parchment is laid to dry on raised beds. Workers rake parchment frequently to ensure even drying. They cover drying parchment during the hottest time of day, to maintain slow, even drying and at night, to shelter parchment from moisture. It takes approximately 14 days for parchment to dry.

Diego Bermudez | Finca El Paraíso

This is not just coffee.

In the cup:

Pink Bourbon - Diego Bermudez - Double Anaerobic Thermal Shock
products.body_html:
Colombia Pink Bourbon Washed Double Anaerobic Thermal Shock
Diego Bermudez | Finca El Paraíso

From Finca El Paraíso in Cauca, Colombia, Diego Bermudez continues to redefine what “washed coffee” can be.

Grown at high elevation in a tightly controlled farm environment, this Pink Bourbon lot represents a shift from traditional farming into process-driven flavour design — where every variable is intentional, repeatable, and engineered for clarity.

Process: Washed, Rebuilt From Scratch

This is not a classic washed coffee.
It’s a high-intervention washed process built on fermentation science.

Process Flow

  • Hand-harvested cherries at peak ripeness
  • Ozone sterilisation to reset microbial activity
  • Primary anaerobic fermentation (~48 hours)
  • Depulping, followed by controlled fermentation with custom microbial cultures
  • Pressurised tank fermentation with recirculated leachates
  • Thermal shock wash to stabilise and lock flavour
  • Controlled low-temperature drying

This layered fermentation approach is designed to construct flavour, not just reveal it .

🌱 Variety: Pink Bourbon, High Expression

Pink Bourbon is not your typical Bourbon mutation — it’s now understood to be genetically closer to Ethiopian landrace varieties, known for:

  • Elevated floral aromatics
  • Complex fruit expression
  • High sweetness potential

It’s one of the most responsive varieties to advanced fermentation — making it the perfect canvas for Diego’s processing style .

Cup Experience: Structured Exotic

Expect a profile that feels engineered but natural:

  • Peach, lychee, and tropical fruit
  • Citrus brightness with floral lift
  • Creamy, almost tea-like texture
  • Long, clean, perfumed finish

This is a washed coffee with unusual depth and saturation, balancing clarity with intensity .

Why This Coffee Hits Different

Because it challenges the idea of washed coffee:

  • Clean, but not simple
  • Sweet, but not heavy
  • Complex, but controlled

You’re tasting:

  • Precision fermentation
  • Repeatable flavour engineering
  • A new category of “modern washed” coffee

Brewing Mindset

Treat this as a high-extraction capable washed coffee:

  • Push extraction for maximum clarity and florals
  • Slightly finer grind enhances sweetness
  • Performs exceptionally well across filter and espresso

This coffee rewards intention — and gives back detail.

The Bigger Picture

Diego Bermudez isn’t just producing coffee — he’s building a processing system that redefines how flavour can be created at origin.

This Pink Bourbon is a benchmark of that philosophy:

Clean.
Precise.
Designed.

products.title: Rwanda - Fugi Washing Station - Anaerobic Natural
products.body_html:
Flavor Notes:  Mango - Strawberry - Tropical Fruit - Crisp Acidity - Milk Chocolate

Producer - Emmanuel Rusatira from BAHO Coffee Company
Variety - Red Bourbon
Process type - Natural Anaerobic
Altitude range - 1550m - 1850m
Harvest period - 2024

We've scored this coffee at SCA Score : 88 Points

FUGI Cws is located along the Akanyaru border of Rwanda and Burundi in the southern province. It is one of the hilliest areas of the country. Agriculture is the main activity practiced in that area and coffee takes a big percentage of the crops cultivated. Baho coffee company processes its cherries using the natural process to bring out the best grade of coffee that will bring out the smiles to every face that graces that region. We use a blend of skilled professional coffee experts led by Emmanuel Rusatira, an experienced coffee certified master, a person you will love beyond coffee, About Baho Coffee
With more than 15 years of experience in the Rwandan speciality coffee industry, the Rusatira family found the opportunity to set up our own four coffee washing stations. The location and specific management of each station show itself in unique flavour profiles. We developed our own grading system and are continuously experimenting with washed, honey, and natural processed coffee. All year round we work together with coffee producers to support them on the field, and financially, so as to produce the best coffee cherries of the region and boost quality year after year. All our attention goes to the selection, de-pulping, fermentation, washing, drying, storage, and continuous quality control.

“Baho means "stay alive" or  "be strong", "don't give up". It is the kind of thing you say to friends when they tell you of their misfortunes or problems. When they want to give up. You hug them and say "Baho!". You give them comfort. This is what I aim to achieve with my company and the coffees we produce, to give comfort to the ones who drink it and the ones who grow it. It is something that is deeply connected to my personal history as a genocide survivor and to the journey of coffee. Coffee is a crop that goes through many difficulties. It is hit by the weather, by bad management,  then you pick it, heat if with fire…  If you could ask coffee to tell you its journey you’d cry. I believe coffee can, in fact, speak. And for me, it says something like... Baho.”along with the uniquely crafted processes to produce this up for all coffee roasters across the world.

products.title: Rwanda - Vunga - Natural
products.body_html:
Vunga, Rwanda

Perched in the rolling hills of Rwanda’s Western Province, Vunga is a region where high altitude, volcanic soils, and cool mountain conditions create the ideal environment for producing vibrant, fruit-driven coffees. Smallholder farmers cultivate coffee on steep slopes, where slow cherry maturation develops concentrated sugars and remarkable flavour complexity.

Rwandan naturals remain relatively rare, making lots like this a showcase of both origin character and careful processing.

Process: Natural, Done Right

Natural coffees can be extraordinary when precision meets patience — and Vunga is a perfect example.

Process Flow

  • Selective hand-picking of fully ripe cherries
  • Careful sorting and density selection
  • Slow drying on raised African beds
  • Regular turning to ensure even moisture reduction
  • Careful monitoring throughout drying and storage

The goal is simple: amplify sweetness and fruit character while preserving clarity and balance.

Variety: Bourbon

Produced from traditional Red Bourbon varieties, this coffee benefits from one of East Africa’s most celebrated genetic lineages.

Bourbon is known for:

  • Dense sweetness
  • Elegant acidity
  • Exceptional cup complexity
  • Outstanding performance at high elevations

When paired with natural processing, Bourbon delivers a cup that is both expressive and refined.

Cup Experience: Fruit-Forward Elegance

Expect a profile that balances juicy sweetness with remarkable cleanliness:

  • Ripe berry notes
  • Stone fruit sweetness
  • Floral aromatics
  • Silky body
  • Lingering sweet finish

This is a natural coffee with structure — vibrant and expressive without becoming overwhelming.

Why Coffee Nerds Love Rwandan Naturals

Rwanda’s combination of high elevation, Bourbon varieties, and meticulous post-harvest processing creates naturals that often feel more refined than their counterparts elsewhere.

You get:

  • The sweetness of a natural

  • Bright East African acidity
  • Excellent balance and drinkability

Think fruit intensity with precision.

Brewing Mindset

This coffee thrives when sweetness and clarity are allowed to shine:

  • Filter brewing highlights fruit complexity and florals
  • Espresso produces syrupy sweetness and berry-forward intensity
  • Slightly higher extraction reveals additional layers of fruit and structure

The Bigger Picture

Rwanda Vunga Natural reflects the evolution of modern Rwandan coffee — where careful processing, smallholder dedication, and exceptional growing conditions come together to produce coffees that are both approachable and captivating.

Sweet.
Elegant.
Beautifully expressive.

products.body_html:
Uganda Nyabirongo Anaerobic Natural

This exceptional anaerobic natural coffee comes from the Nyabirongo community in the Rwenzori region of Uganda, an area increasingly recognised for producing some of East Africa’s most expressive and high-quality coffees. Crafted by dedicated smallholder farmers and processed with precision, this lot showcases the bold fruit character and complexity that anaerobic naturals are celebrated for.

Origin & Community

  • Producer: Nyabirongo Community

  • Region: Nyabirongo, Rwenzori Mountains

  • Country: Uganda

  • Altitude: 1300–1600 MASL

The Nyabirongo community is known for its commitment to quality-focused coffee production. Cherries are grown on fertile mountain slopes and carefully hand-picked at peak ripeness by smallholder farmers, ensuring consistency and clarity in the final cup.

UGANDA NYABIRONGO ANAEROBIC NATURAL

Process: Anaerobic Natural (Underwater Fermentation)

This coffee undergoes a distinctive natural underwater fermentation process that enhances sweetness, fruit intensity, and aromatic complexity:

  1. Ripe cherries are hand-selected and submerged in water

  2. Fermented anaerobically for 48 hours

  3. Slowly sun-dried and turned by hand to ensure even drying

  4. Hulled, cleaned, and carefully sorted at the dry mill

  5. Stored in GrainPro bags to preserve freshness and quality

This controlled fermentation environment allows flavour compounds to develop more fully, resulting in a vibrant and layered cup profile

UGANDA NYABIRONGO ANAEROBIC NATURAL.

Coffee Variety

  • SL28

  • SL14

These classic East African varieties are prized for their bright acidity, complex fruit notes, and elegant structure, making them ideal candidates for anaerobic processing

Flavour Profile

Expect a lively and fruit-forward cup with a clean yet expressive finish. Typical characteristics include:

  • Ripe red and tropical fruits

  • Jammy sweetness

  • Floral aromatics

  • Balanced acidity with a smooth, rounded body

The anaerobic natural process amplifies intensity while maintaining clarity, making this coffee both adventurous and approachable.

Why This Coffee Stands Out

  • Rare Ugandan anaerobic natural

  • Meticulously hand-processed by a renowned farming community

  • Ideal for filter, pour-over, espresso, and cold brew

  • Showcases Uganda’s rising status in specialty coffee

products.title: V60 2 Cup
products.body_html:
The Hario V60 Coffee Dripper has been at the epicentre of the surging interest in speciality coffee in South Africa and across the world. It embodies the movement that has (re)embraced hand-brewed coffee alongside the more traditional espresso-based coffee culture. Specifically, the Hario V60 belongs to the increasingly popular family of pour-over coffee makers.

This simple, beautifully engineered little cone allows delicious coffee to be made easily and affordably, without the need for an expensive machine. While additional pieces of equipment like drip kettles and servers may help a little, all you really need to make a fantastic brew with a V60 Coffee Dripper is a kettle to heat water, fresh coffee and a cup to stand it on.

The style of coffee the V60 makes is very different from espresso - a nod to the past as much as it is a part of a new world of coffee. It is filter coffee but filter coffee made with precise control over brewing variables, allowing the natural flavours of the coffee you're drinking to shine. This tendency to highlight, rather than alter, the coffee's characteristics explains why it has been adopted by many roasters of high quality, single origin coffee beans all over the world.

If you're an adventurous coffee drinker who likes to explore different flavours and experiment with brewing variables, the Hario V60 Coffee Dripper is an essential piece of coffee equipment to own.

 

Source Cape Coffee Beans

products.title: Wooden Coffee Paper Filter Holder
products.body_html: Are your coffee filters always cluttering your counter? Keep them neatly stored and within easy reach with this beautifully crafted wooden paper filter holder. Designed to fit most pour-over and percolation filters, this stylish accessory adds a touch of warmth to your brew station while providing a practical storage solution. Perfect for manual brewers who value both function and aesthetics, it keeps your filters clean, organised, and ready for your next brew.
